subject: tool:webfrank
value: WEBFRANK'S STACK-POINTER REFUSAL IS A CATEGORICAL CLASS BOUNDARY, NOT A DEPENDENCE FINDING, AND IT IS STAGE-INDEPENDENT -- so neither the post-recolor stage nor a window split can route around it, and a lane that reads its message as a fact about its function will re-derive the wrong diagnosis. THE MECHANISM, read from the source rather than inferred: check_permutation_dependences opens with a per-atom loop containing `if ("g", 1) in writes: raise ValueError(f"atom {index}: permutation region redefines r1")`, which fires BEFORE the per-resource def-use analysis in the same function. Any region containing a stack-pointer adjust is refused whatever else is in it. MEASURED on game/enemy/critter::CritterDamagePlayer at 84f85a96a, whose 68/68 residual is 6 recolor words plus a 4-word epilogue in which ours emits `lfd f31,56(r1)` / `lmw r28,40(r1)` / `addi r1,r1,64` / `mtlr r0` and the target emits `lmw` / `lfd` / `mtlr` / `addi` -- two independent adjacent transpositions. THREE shapes were run through the shipped apply_patch and all three were refused with the same message: two windows (`atom 0`), one 4-atom window with order [1,0,3,2] (`atom 2`), and the two windows moved to the POST-RECOLOR stage (`atom 0`). THE LAST OF THOSE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. claim.law.C1_permute-recolor-composition-needs-a-permutation-legal-in-our-colouring.20260901.v1 and unpermute_target_windows exist precisely so a permutation illegal in our colouring can run in the target's, and that device closed MBWorldToScreen3D's cluster B in this same run -- but it does NOT help here, because the r1 gate is not about colouring at all. Isolating each half against check_permutation_dependences directly: window 0xfc:0x104 (`lfd`/`lmw`) is ACCEPTED and its permutation reproduces the target slice exactly; window 0x104:0x10c (`addi r1,r1,64` / `mtlr r0`) is REFUSED at atom 0. Applying only the accepted window leaves 8 differing words, so no partial rule closes the function. THE REFUSAL IS COARSE AND THE COARSENESS IS DELIBERATE, which is the distinction AGENTS.md discipline 14 asks for and which decides who may act on it. The finer analysis in the very same function would accept this swap: `_word_effects` reports `addi r1,r1,64` as reads={('g',1)} writes={('g',1)} and `mtlr r0` as reads={('g',0)} writes={'lr'} -- no shared resource -- and both r1-relative loads sit ABOVE the adjust in BOTH orders, so the frame is live when they read it either way, with the `blr` outside the region. But the blanket form is pinned by tools/gdl/tests/test_webfrank.py::test_a_permutation_region_redefining_r1_is_refused, whose comment states the reason ('Reordering a region that redefines r1 moves every r1-relative access in it onto a different frame, so the permutation class refuses the region outright'), and t8_refusal_coverage.py classes it PINNED rather than listing it among the 12 unpinned BOUNDARY refusals. THE DEMAND IS NOT ZERO, so this is a proposal rather than a refuted premise: an image-wide census (tools/gdl/composed_census/ws_r1_demand_census.py, founding run 3b2e17c46) over 3316 paired equal-size functions finds 598 differing and 48 whose residual touches an r1-writing word -- a deliberate UPPER bound, since it does not check that a permutation would close them. The rows sharing CritterDamagePlayer's small adjacent-epilogue shape include game/ui/btext::FontHeight (10 differing words, r1 at 0x4c/0x50), dolphin/dvd/dvdlow::AlarmForWA and ::AlarmForTimeout (10 each), game/ps2/fakelib::sDvdReadSync (5) and game/boss/boss::HealthMeterStart (12). THE STANDING RULE, and the reason this is a law rather than a note: a lane meeting `permutation region redefines r1` has NOT measured its function. It has measured the class boundary, and the correct deliverable is an instrumented refusal record plus this census row, never a rule shipped by loosening the gate -- the Mandatory result policy sends class-boundary proposals to the integrator, and the frame/ABI surface is the last place a lane should relax one unilaterally.
